questions.question: What does 'cumulative car-laps' mean as the intra-session evolution index -- field-total laps or per-car laps?
questions.resolution: Field-wide cumulative_track_laps (ALL cars, count of lap_number < X), NOT per-car. Already implemented in src/physics/layer2/session_race.py:268 compute_cumulative_track_laps(session_id, first_clean_lap_num, db_path). G reuses this exact counting convention, vectorized per-session rather than called per-lap.

questions.question: Which session_types does G's fit cover, given tyre_supplant.py's correction machinery is hardcoded to session_type='R'?
questions.resolution: G's fit runs uniformly across ALL session types (FP1/FP2/FP3/Q/SQ/R/S); tyre_supplant._read_clean_race_laps's session_type='R' filter is generalized to a parameter. No blanket type exclusion -- the #560 thin-session rule (q3) catches structurally-thin sessions (mostly Q/SQ in practice) case-by-case instead.
questions.human_answer: Self-resolved per LAUNCH_ORDER-663.md Inherited Latitude ('your own fit/test decisions' is explicitly in-latitude); grounded in real 2023 DB stint-length/compound-diversity measurement (Q median 2 laps/stint, 76.8% thin; FP1-3/R structurally adequate). No epic-wide ramification identified -- not floated to the Admiral.

questions.question: #560: what does G do with a session too thin to fit?
questions.resolution: Wide-sigma fallback, never silent skip -- reuses the same mechanism already named for the rain-flag case. Floor: >=2 usable driver-stints with >=MIN_STINT_LAPS(4, reused from tyre_supplant) laps each; below that, offset comes from nearest-neighbor within-weekend extrapolation with inflated sigma. 2023 incidence measured directly per session type (FP1 35.0%, FP2 36.4%, FP3 52.1%, Q 76.8%, R 11.4%, SQ 58.7%, S 2.2% of driver-stints thin).
questions.human_answer: Self-resolved per LAUNCH_ORDER-663.md Pre-Ruling decision:thin-session-explicit, which explicitly assigns this choice to the Commander ('you MUST decide explicitly...Choose a rule...float only if epic-wide'). No epic-wide ramification identified (SegmentMap/#661 and other consumers untouched) -- not floated.

questions.question: Held-out reconciliation gate: what is the disjoint driver/lap split axis and scheme?
questions.resolution: Driver-based ~50/50 split (stratified by team where available), verified feasible: 2023 DB has median 20 drivers/session (min 15) across all session types. Fit G on fit-set drivers' laps only; score cross-session same-driver/compound/similar-fuel reconciliation error on held-out drivers, with vs without subtracting G.
questions.human_answer: Self-resolved per LAUNCH_ORDER-663.md Inherited Latitude ('your own fit/test decisions'); the held-out-not-in-sample REQUIREMENT itself is settled/human (decision:held-out-not-in-sample) -- only the concrete split mechanics were mine to choose, grounded in real driver-count data.

questions.question: Synthetic-recovery test: what quantitative criterion counts as 'separable'?
questions.resolution: (a) Parameter recovery: >=90% of >=50 synthetic replicates land within the fit's own reported 2-sigma predictive interval of injected ground truth (calibration, not just point-bias). (b) Separability: fit's estimated curve-initial-value/offset correlation magnitude < 0.8 (frozen threshold) in >=90% of replicates. Falsified if either fails at the stated rate.
questions.human_answer: Self-resolved per LAUNCH_ORDER-663.md Inherited Latitude; the REQUIREMENT for a synthetic-recovery separability test is settled/human (decision:synthetic-identifiability) -- only the concrete pass/fail threshold was mine to choose, following the repo's precedented LOO/calibration discipline (lesson:loo-residual-diagnostic-over-self-weighted-predictor).
